method: Treat the route start A, route end B and position P as unit vectors on a sphere of mean radius 6,371 km. The route length is the central angle between A and B; identical endpoints and antipodal endpoints are refused because no single course exists. The cross-track angle is minus the arcsine of P's component along the unit normal of the A-B great circle, which is positive when P lies to the right (starboard) of the course. P is projected onto the great circle by removing that normal component, and the signed along-track angle is measured from A toward B with atan2 so that a position behind the start is negative and a position past the destination exceeds the route length. The nearest point on the route is the projection, clamped to the start when the along-track angle is negative and to the destination when it exceeds the route length; distance to the route is the central angle from P to that point. Distance still to run is the remaining route angle clamped at zero. Coordinates are decimal degrees accepted with a decimal point or comma, latitude from -90 to 90 and longitude from -180 to 180; blank, non-numeric, exponent-notation and out-of-range values are refused with the failing field named. The model is spherical and ignores ellipsoidal flattening, magnetic variation, currents, leeway, rhumb-line courses and terrain, and results within half a metre of the track are reported as on track.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Great-circle navigation: cross-track distance is the angular distance from a point to a great-circle path, and along-track distance is measured from the start of the path toward the destination.

Ed Williams, Aviation Formulary: the spherical cross-track formula asin(sin(d13) sin(theta13 - theta12)) and the along-track formula acos(cos(d13) / cos(xtd)), with positive cross-track conventionally to starboard.
NOAA Chart No. 1 and nautical navigation practice: cross-track error is the perpendicular offset between a vessel's position and its intended track, reported to port or starboard of the course.
